data_fields.name: xp_threshold_for_level
data_fields.donor_constant: base table of 50 entries: 10, 25, 45, 70 ... 4500000 used (5000000 unused); threshold = base x expfact / 100

data_fields.name: expfact_percent
data_fields.donor_constant: race exp + class exp (Human race 100; class part not set in active class file)

data_fields.name: monster_base_xp
data_fields.donor_constant: monster mexp (per monster, table not read)

data_fields.name: kill_xp_level_divisor
data_fields.donor_constant: player level (kill XP = mexp x monster level / player level)

data_fields.name: high_water_gain_fraction
data_fields.donor_constant: 1/10 of each gain while behind the mark

best_idea: Keep a high-water XP mark so a drain lowers current XP but not the mark, and while behind the mark each gain raises the mark by a tenth; and carry the fraction of each kill's XP so small rewards are never lost to rounding.
decision_why: Take the fractional carry and the level-gap kill formula now; the high-water mark adds a second XP number to the one ledger, so it waits for a row 17 death-penalty decision.
acceptance: After +1000 XP and a non-permanent -500 drain the mark stays 1000; +100 then gives 600 XP and mark 1010; two kills of base 10 at monster level 5 by a level 3 character credit 16 then 17 XP.
